correctness.rationale: Each edge has its own central bracket, so [x,y]=0 if and only if all edge determinants vanish; on support this fixes one ratio per induced connected component, forces neighbor-outside coefficients to zero, and leaves b(S) free. Rank-nullity yields exact rank for all fields, and independent projective-direction counting over F_q gives the commuting-pair Q evaluation. Exhaustive direct edge-equation and Gaussian-elimination checks on all graphs of sizes <=4 over F2/F3 and <=3 over F4, plus wider polynomial and tree tests, returned VERIFY_OK. Finite tests support but do not replace the proof; all boundary cases and characteristics are covered algebraically.

value.rationale: A complete formula for every element-centralizer dimension in the graph Lie family is a natural algebraic structural classification with arbitrary graph size, not a one-off numerical improvement. It determines the full distribution of adjoint ranks (hence all centralizer sizes) over every finite field and identifies the exact commutativity invariant with an independently established graph polynomial; forests inherit an efficient evaluation. The Lie-theoretic result goes beyond previously established general degree averaging, rigid graph classification, and graph Q computations.
